Dialogue.Page: Oh me oh my! The sun is loosing stability! I can see it on my telescope! If nothing is done about this, we are toast!
Oh me oh my! Is that... our planet... in the sky... above our planet?
Well, this doesn't change that the sun is continuing to lose stability...

DialogueOption.Text: Hey Corey, could you send the 'Go' signal to launch the Sun Stabilisation Devices on both planets?
Hey Corey, could you send the 'Go' signal to launch the Sun Stabilisation Devices on both planets?

Dialogue.Page: Oh sorry, I didn't see you there! Welcome to the North pole. This area serves both as our observatory and our radio communications centre.
You know, for communiating with objects in space, such as our sun monitoring probe. If there are any other planets out there that are close enough, maybe we could call them for help...

DialogueOption.Text: Are there any plans to save the sun?

Dialogue.Page: I heard Bruce was working on a sun stabilisation device in the equatorial dry dock. Though it sounds like he needs more time to get it working well enough to save the sun...
Fortuitously, I've also heard someone was working on some time travel project down on the South pole. Maybe that could buy us the time we need to figure out this sun situation...?
The future one is not responding. Is older Bruce okay...?
Bruce is saying that the Temporal Displacement Device on the South pole needs to be disabled first.
Alright! Bruce and Bruce are confirming that they are launching!
Oh me oh my! The sun is finally stable! I can see it on my telescope! We are saved!
